facts.timeline_arc: June 2025 saw Amazon fade from the headlines, but by July the company was drawn into broader climate emergencies and terror‑financing warnings targeting e‑commerce platforms. In August a tragic death in a Phoenix fulfillment center and a sharp rise in Brazilian rainforest deforestation amplified scrutiny of Amazon’s safety and sustainability commitments. The following months featured a shooting at a Georgia warehouse, new data showing extensive forest loss, and a controversial expansion of cloud data centers in Oregon, while the company also pursued AI talent in January. Early 2026 brought a shocking child‑abuse case in Brazil’s Amazonas and renewed climate policy battles, and by April and May renewed labor‑safety concerns surfaced with a warehouse worker collapse and a fatal delivery‑van accident.

turning_points.why: Amazon became linked to rising climate emergencies and terror‑financing concerns affecting e‑commerce platforms.
A fatal incident in a fulfillment center and a 61.8% jump in Brazilian deforestation heightened safety and sustainability pressures.
Amazon expanded its data‑center footprint in Oregon, sparking local environmental and community worries.
The company announced a strategic deal to secure AI talent, signaling a push into the fast‑moving AI race.
A warehouse worker collapsed on the floor, reviving concerns over labor conditions and employee health.
A 4‑year‑old child was killed by an Amazon delivery van, prompting renewed scrutiny of driver training and safety protocols.

text.summary: Amazon generated 721,091 articles in the window from 2024-06 to 2026-05, of which 236,395 fall in the top priority bands. That places it second among the four companies compared on attention, with a 26.2% share against 35.3% for Google. Attention over the latest three months (105,951 articles) was above the previous three months (85,223), a ratio of 1.24. Tone is comparatively mild: negative-to-positive stories stand at 0.3 in the latest three months, against 0.27 for the whole window and 0.58 for all news. Artificial intelligence, at 65,513 articles and 8.44% of company coverage, is the largest catalyst section shown, ahead of AWS at 31,230 articles. Recent coverage has also carried operational and safety stories, including warehouse and delivery incidents.
text.signals: Attention rose, with 105,951 articles in March to May 2026 against 85,223 in the prior three months. Tone stayed close to the company's own norm, at 0.3 negative per positive against 0.29 before. Risk events rose to 166 in the latest six months from 100, while catalyst events fell to 268 from 347.
text.themes_time: Technology rose from 27.8% in 2021 to 34.1% in 2025. Entertainment stood at 10.8% in 2021 and does not appear in the 2025 figures, and movies went from 3.0% in 2021 to no listed share in 2025. Consumer electronics rose from 4.2% to 8.5%, retail from 4.6% to 6.8%, and shopping from 0.8% to 2.2%. E-commerce moved from 2.5% to 3.3%, and cloud computing from 1.0% to 1.1%, while finance (6.6%) and economy (4.8%) appear only in 2021.
text.lenses: AI is the largest lens by articles at 65,513 (8.44% of coverage), followed by Product at 41,836 (5.8%) and Marketing at 19,539 (2.71%). Finance, at 7,636 articles, grew most between early and late periods (late-versus-early 2.35), with AI next at 1.92. Legal and regulatory is the smallest lens at 3,850 articles but by far the most negative, at 11.7 negative per positive, while Partnerships (0.07) and Product (0.09) are the least negative.
text.peers: Amazon's coverage is more concentrated in technology (56.1%), consumer electronics (14.5%) and retail (10.8%) than that of Apple, Microsoft or Google; its e-commerce share is 5.6% against 0.5% for Apple and 0.4% for Google. Peers show shares in AI (Apple 1.6%, Microsoft 2.9%, Google 4.1%), software and, for Google, politics (9.9%), none of which are listed for Amazon in this comparison. Amazon's attention growth of 1.17 is labelled flat, whereas Google's 1.65 is rising, and Amazon's tone of 0.27 negative per positive is the mildest of the four.
text.mix: Risk events in the latest six months centred on lawsuits, regulatory matters and layoffs, while catalyst events centred on new products, contracts, M&A, asset acquisitions and job creation. There were also 50 earnings events and 46 key-people events, and tone runs well below the 0.58 seen across all news.
text.events: Recent events include the opening of Amazon Supply Chain Services, free same-day grocery delivery for Prime business members on orders over $25, and a fulfilment centre and a $51 million distribution centre expected to bring 500 jobs. On the people side, Neil Lindsay is stepping down as head of Amazon Health. Unsealed filings in a 2026 antitrust trial allege Amazon pressured brands over pricing on other retail sites, and an expanded contract with Sam Altman's lead firm was reported.
text.risks: Layoffs (5,944 articles) and antitrust (2,943 articles) are the tracked risk sections, both strongly negative at 4.1 and 4.87 negative per positive; layoffs coverage grew 5.71 times from the first to last third while antitrust coverage was 0.38. Safety and labour stories, including a fatal fulfilment-centre incident, a warehouse collapse and a fatal delivery-van accident, plus environmental concern over Oregon data centres, add operational scrutiny.
text.catalysts: AI (65,513 articles, 1.92 late-versus-first) and AWS (31,230 articles, 1.69) both grew and sit near the company's tone norm, at 0.28 and 0.22 negative per positive. Contracts, new products and the January 2026 deal to secure AI talent are the visible catalyst types, though catalyst events fell to 268 from 347.
text.areas: Activity centres on shopping portals, coupons and discount offers, and product reviews and price comparisons. It also covers small kitchen appliances, media streaming devices and home automation.
text.timeline: Coverage in mid-2025 turned to climate and terror-financing concerns for e-commerce platforms, then to a fatal fulfilment-centre incident and Brazilian deforestation in August. Oregon data-centre expansion in December and an AI talent deal in January 2026 followed, and April and May 2026 brought renewed labour-safety stories.
